**Public handoff — General_Hospital_Surgery → General_Hospital_Ward, St_Marys_Center_Ward**

Colleagues, two patients remain: Patient_3 (GH) and Patient_7 (St_Marys). Each hospital holds exactly one Pain_Killers unit, and Ward care consumes it. Please treat that unit as reserved for your own pending patient — do not move it.

**General_Hospital_Ward (planning43):** Patient_3 finishes Surgery at t=20, so your Ward step must start at 20 and run 48h. Keep your Pain_Killers in place; a transfer out would leave Patient_3 unrescuable, and a return after execution52 is too late. If you want extra margin, request resupply from Resource_Provisioner rather than shipping your own kit away — native transfers add 15 credit per unit moved even when unnecessary, so a swap costs you and gains nothing clinically.

**St_Marys_Center_Ward (planning44):** Patient_7 has only Triage done; schedule the Ward step at your execution turn and hold your Pain_Killers for it. Same logic: do not send your kit to the other hospital on the theory of a later return — there is no guaranteed return and no scripted cooperation, and a kit sent after GH execution52 cannot restore that missed last opportunity.

**On coordination:** I know cross-hospital pooling looks attractive, but with one kit per site and both patients pending, the only robust plan is each Ward serving its own queue. A single recipient holding two kits could theoretically rescue both, but that requires a voluntary handoff with no enforcement and no return guarantee — too fragile to rely on. Prefer the local, resource-valid path.

**Execution turns (52/53):** schedule your pending patient's Ward step first, confirm the common supply preflight passes, and only then consider any transfer. If preflight rejects, do not resubmit blindly — check the kit is still native.

Care first: one kit, one patient, each site.

**Public handoff — General_Hospital_Surgery → General_Hospital_Ward, St_Marys_Center_Ward**

Two patients remain: Patient_3 (GH) and Patient_7 (St_Marys). Each hospital holds exactly one Pain_Killers unit. The cleanest path is for each Ward to schedule its own pending patient in execution, consuming its native kit. That closes both cases without cross-hospital transfers.

A few cautions before you commit:

- **Don't rush the transfer reflex.** Moving a kit across hospitals adds 15 credit per unit moved and creates a dependency on the other site's timing. If the receiving Ward then has to return or re-source, you've added coordination risk for no clinical gain. Native scheduling is simpler and self-contained.
- **Reserve discipline matters more than speed.** The common supply preflight will reject a deficient proposal outright — no state mutation, no failure increment — so a rejected batch just burns your turn. Verify the full resource set (Pain_Killers plus the other items shown in state) before scheduling, rather than firing early and re-planning.
- **Consider whether both Wards need to act this round.** If one site schedules and the other waits, you preserve flexibility and avoid two simultaneous transfers competing for the same logistics. There's no scripted return and no guaranteed cooperation, so a plan that assumes a kit comes back is fragile.
- **Credit-seeking coordination is a trap here.** Chasing transfer rewards by shuffling kits between sites increases failure surface without improving patient outcomes. The objective is complete care, not ledger movement.

My recommendation: each Ward schedules its own pending patient natively in execution, using its own kit, with the full resource set confirmed first. If a transfer is genuinely unavoidable, do it once, deliberately, and only after confirming the receiving site can actually complete the step — not speculatively.
